s1Design.before: `computeDamageBarData` computed `totalDamage = destroyedComponents.length * 2 + destroyedLocations.length * 4` and the whole damage block was gated on `totalDamage > 0`. A unit with real armor loss and no destroyed component rendered identically to a unit at full health.
s1Design.after: `IDamageBarData` carries `damagePercent: number | null` and `maximaUnavailable: boolean` in place of `totalDamage`. `computeDamagePercent` sums the armor and structure points named by `IUnitMaxState` and the points still present in `IUnitCombatState`, clamping each per-location loss to [0, max]; locations the max-state does not name are skipped, matching `buildTicketsFromUnitState`'s unknown-maximum rule. A max-state with no positive points returns null ('unknown', not '0% damaged'). The `useDamageBarData` selector now also reads `state.campaign?.unitMaxStates?.[unitId]` inside the SAME subscription, and its shallow-equality memo compares `damagePercent` + `maximaUnavailable` instead of `totalDamage`.
s1Design.render: The bar renders only when `damagePercent !== null && damagePercent > 0`, with the width set to the percentage and a `data-testid="roster-unit-damage-percent"` label. When `maximaUnavailable` is true the card renders a `data-testid="roster-unit-damage-unavailable"` row reading 'Maxima unavailable'. Neither branch ever shows a stock maximum or a 0% placeholder.
s1Design.readinessUntouched: `getReadinessStyles`, `unit.readiness`, and the 'Needs Repair' block were not modified. Verified by the row-(e) regression guard and by the diff (b325ae191 touches only the damage-bar shape, the selector, and the two render branches).

whereTheAuthorityIsCalled.resolver: src/lib/campaign/maxState/unitMaxStateResolver.ts - `resolveUnitMaxState` calls `adaptUnit(unitRef, {}, readCustom)` from `src/engine/adapters/CompendiumAdapter.ts`. That is the SAME entry point combat launch uses (`deriveCombatSeededGameUnits` in `src/engine/combatSeedDerivation.ts:56`), and it is where the canonical/custom split already lives: `custom-` refs go to `CustomUnitDefinitionReader` (browser default `customUnitApiService.getById`; server `readServerCustomCombatDefinition` is injectable through the optional `readCustom` parameter), every other ref to `getCanonicalUnitService().getById`. `adaptUnit` is called with no `initialDamage`, so `adapted.armor` / `adapted.structure` / `adapted.ammo` are construction values.

The `'CT'`/`'LT'` examples in the `IUnitMaxState` doc comment are aspirational and do not match runtime data; that comment was NOT edited (out of the minimum diff), and is listed as an open question.

howMissingDesignsStayUnavailable: No `unitRef` on the roster projection -> `null`, no entry.

Ref contradicts the recorded `unitSource` (canonical source with a `custom-` ref, or custom source with a non-`custom-` ref), or `parseRosterUnitSource` reports `invalid` -> `null`, no entry, and the other authority is never consulted. Mirrors `admitCanonicalExactReference`'s `source_ref_mismatch` denial.

Deleted or invalid custom design -> `adaptUnit` THROWS ('Saved custom unit ... is missing, invalid or unsupported for combat.'); the resolver catches and returns `null` -> no entry. The throw is caught per-unit, so one unresolvable design does not poison the rest of the batch (covered by a test row).
Nothing is ever substituted: there is no stock fallback path in the resolver, and mutant S2-M1 proves the tests detect one if added.
A unit with no entry falls through to S1's explicit 'Maxima unavailable' affordance on the card.
s2PopulationDesign.idempotence: `resolveMissingUnitMaxStates` skips any unit that already has an entry, so an existing pinned construction snapshot is never re-derived and a repeat call resolves nothing and writes nothing.

persistenceAnswer.evidence: `unitMaxStates` is already carried both ways on both persistence paths, read directly this session: server envelope serialize `src/lib/campaign/persistence/serializeCampaign.ts:166` and deserialize `:236`; localStorage persist `src/stores/campaign/useCampaignStore.persistence.ts:288` and rehydrate `:381`. It is declared optional on both `ICampaign` (`src/types/campaign/Campaign.ts:162`) and `SerializedCampaign` (`src/types/campaign/SerializedCampaign.ts:194`). No schema or migration change was added.

s2PopulationDesign.dirtyFlagNote: On the campaign-load path the backfill's `updateCampaign` fires the `campaignPersistenceWiring` subscription's `markDirty`, but `runLoad`'s own `set({ dirty: false, ... })` runs afterwards and clears it. Net effect: the backfilled maxima live in the in-memory campaign and are written on the next save rather than triggering an immediate autosave. This is deliberate (no write amplification on load) and is safe because the resolution is idempotent and re-runs on every load until the entries persist.

`ensureCampaignUnitMaxStates` is not wired to the Mech Bay refit/re-add flow or to any post-battle path, because no other production site adds a unit to `useCampaignRosterStore`. If a future flow adds one, it must call the same function - there is no subscription-based catch-all.

On the campaign-load path the backfill runs only when `cacheStands` is false (i.e. when the record is actually deserialized). When the live in-memory copy is reused, the backfill is skipped on the assumption it already ran for that copy earlier in the session. That holds for the current load flow but is an assumption, not a proof.
